MADDUR.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FURTHER HEARING, THIS DAY, K.S.MUDAGAL.J, DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT "Whether the compensation awarded to the appellant under the impugned award is just one? is the question involved in this case".
2.
The appellant is the owner of land bearing Sy.No.2 of Shivapura village measuring 18 guntas and land bearing Sy.No.436/1 of Chamenahalli village measuring 11 guntas.
The said lands were acquired for the purpose of formation of Bengaluru-Mysuru two lanes of Railway broad gauge line.
The preliminary notification was issued on 15.12.1990 that was published in a Gazette on 31.01.1991.

The final notification was issued on 30.04.1991 and published in the official gazette on 07.11.1991.
3.
Thereafter, the first respondent - the Land Acquisition Officer passed the general award on 02.11.1992.
Respondent No.1 awarded Rs.12,304/- for 11 guntas in Sy.No.436/1 and Rs.46,190.15 to 18 guntas in Sy.No.2.
So far as lands in Sy.No.2 and Sy.No.436/1, the compensation was awarded at the rate of Rs.820/- per gunta.
For 26 coconut trees in Sy.No.2, compensation of Rs.46,190.15/- was awarded and in Sy.No.436/1 Rs.1000/- per coconut tree was awarded.
4. The award notice was issued to the appellant on 12.03.1993.

On the application of the appellant under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, the matter was referred to the Senior Civil Judge,

sentences.text: The appellant claimed that the acquired lands are situated within the limits of Maddur Town Municipal Council, therefore they had commercial value.
Therefore the compensation awarded is on the lower side.
5. Respondents contested the claim petition denying that the property had the commercial value or the same situated within the limits of Municipal Council, Maddur.
They further denied the market value as asserted by the claimant.
6. To substantiate his claim, claimant got himself examined as PW.1 and got three other witnesses as PWs.2 to 4.
On his behalf Exs.P1 to 27 were marked.
Respondents did not lead any evidence.
7. The Reference Court on hearing the parties by the impugned award enhanced the compensation to Rs.3999/- per gunta.

The Reference Court relying on the award passed by itself in LAC No.91/2000 pertaining to a land situated within the limits of Bannahalli of C.A Kere Hobli, which was acquired under the notification of 1991-92, awarded compensation of Rs.3,999/-.
8. Sri B.S Mahendra, learned Counsel for the appellant submits that the award in LAC No.91/2000 was not the part of the record and the appellant had no occasion to meet the said award.
He further submits that such approach of the Reference Court in relying on a document which was not part of the record is violative of principles of natural justice.
Referring to Exs.P5 to 12 he submits that for similarly situated lands, the Reference Court had awarded Rs.250/- per Sq.ft and the Reference Court should have followed the same.

9. Per contra Smt. H.R Anitha, learned HCGP for respondent Nos.1 to 3 and Sri Abhinay Y.T,
learned Counsel for respondent No.4 submit that the notification under Exs.P5 to 12 pertained to the year 2000, whereas notification in question was of the year 1991.
Therefore, the Reference Court was justified in not following the said awards.
They submit that the existence of the award in LAC No.91/2000 is not in dispute and the Court was justified in taking judicial notice of the same.
10. The compensation, in case of acquisition of the land has to be determined by the Reference Court having regard to Section 23 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

The above provisions show that in determining the amount of compensation the Court has to take into consideration the market value of the land as on the date of publication of the notification under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act and the loss suffered by the land owner due to taking of standing trees or crops, wells etc.
11. Section 23(1)(A) of the Act states that to the market value of the land as on the date of 4(1)
notification, the market value of 12% has to be added from the date of preliminary notification or from the date of taking possession of the land whichever is earlier.
12.

13. How the market value of the land has to be assessed was dealt with by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Highways Authority of India V/s P. Nagaraju @ Cheluvaiah and another1 in para 32 of the said judgment it was held that for determination of the market value, the rate prevailing prior to the date of the notification shall be the basis more particularly when the determination is made based on sale statistics.

sentences.text: It was further held that if the document proximal to the date of acquisition is not available, then the determination has to be made based on a document taking into consideration the time gap between such document and the date of notification.
For that purpose reasonable de-escalation can be considered.
14. In the present case, though the appellant relied Ex.P19 the sale deed, same pertains to the year 2001, whereas notification was of the year 1991.

Therefore, the Reference Court was justified in not Sri B R Srinivasa Murthy vs The Special Land Acquisition Officer on 15 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46456116/

sentences.text: The appellant did not even produce what was the Sub Register's value of the property during relevant period.
There was no explanation for not producing such documents.
15. Though the appellant relied of Ex.P27 the certificate allegedly issued by the Chief Officer, Town Municipal Council, Maddur, the author of the said document was not examined.
PW.1 the appellant in his cross- examination admitted that he was president of Maddur Town Municipal Council for three terms.
It was contended that using his office he has secured such documents and that was not genuine.
Therefore, the Reference Court was justified in holding that Ex.P27 was of no avail to the appellant.

16. Then the only other documents available were Exs.P5 to 12, the awards in LAC Nos.7/2005,
76/2006, 1/2009 and 2/2009 and order of this Court in MFA Nos.6402/2012, 7767/2012,
7766/2012, 1353/2013, 9388/2012.
The awards in Exs.P5 to 11 related to land situated within the limits of Chamanahalli and Shivapura only.
Therefore they were relevant.
For those lands, Reference Court had awarded compensation of Rs.250/- per Sq.ft.
That means (1089x250) Rs.2,72,250/- per gunta.
However, the notifications of the said award related to the year 2000.
The notification in question was of the year 1991.
Therefore, as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Highways Authority of India's case referred to supra de-escalation for a period of ten years has to be given in the award.

. In another judgment in Chandrashekar (D) by LRs. and others Vs. Land Acquisition Officer and another , the Hon'ble Supreme Court in similar circumstances, approved de-escalation at 10% on account of 'waiting period'.

The Reference Court should have awarded compensation at the rate of Rs.94,743/- per gunta with all other statutory benefits.
However, the appellant has paid Court fee restricting his claim to Rs.57 per Sq.ft.
Compensation has to be paid to him subject to payment of Court fee for enhanced compensation.
Therefore, the appeal deserves to be allowed in part.

Hence, the following:
ORDER
The appeal is partly allowed.

The impugned award is modified as follows:
(i) The market value of the acquired land is fixed at Rs.94,743/- per gunta.
(ii) The enhanced compensation is payable to the appellant/claimant subject to payment of deficit Court fee within four weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is settled law that in determining the market value, the Court has to take into consideration either of the following factors or some of them together:
 (i) Expert's opinion;
 (ii) Sale statistics;
 (iii) Capitalisation method; &
 (iv) Awards passed in respect of similarly situated lands either under the same notification or different notifications.
13. How the market value of the land has to be assessed was dealt with by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Highways Authority of India V/s P. Therefore, the Reference Court should have awarded compensation of Rs.250/- per Sq.ft., on deducting de-escalation at the rate of 10%.
